study type: Cross-sectional comparative study with short observational follow-up
exposure: Type of cesarean section (elective vs. emergency)
outcome: Gastric volume (estimated by antral cross-sectional area)
cohort: The study included 45 parturients in each of two groups (ASAPS II & II E), aged 20 to 35 years, scheduled for either elective or emergency cesarean section under spinal anaesthesia.
finding: The mean antral cross-sectional area was significantly higher in the emergency cesarean group (385.69 mm2) compared to the elective group (237.316 mm2) (p<0.001), and a strong negative correlation was found between NPO status and antral cross-sectional area in both groups, particularly in the emergency group.
mod_finding: Women undergoing emergency cesarean section had a significantly larger estimated gastric volume (higher mean antral cross-sectional area) than those undergoing elective cesarean section.
cross-section timing: 15 minutes prior to spinal anaesthesia administration
